chapter: Germany, Paris and return to America
title: Going out as a soloist in Germany, Switzerland and Belgium
summary: Around 1960 Waters toured as a soloist, lived three and a half years in Hamburg and two in Mannheim, and bought his tax-free car there intending to go home.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe

blocks.x: So we come to the end of - jumpin' back now to the, to following it year by year - you went through a sequence of gigs at La Cigalle. And then for a while you went out
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82 94
on your own to Germany -
Yes, I did. Germany and Switzerland and Belgium.
Were those tours under your own name?
Yeah, I was working as a soloist then.
Right. And that's sort of like the start of the way you've been presenting yourself in Europe for the last 20 years.
[ ], yeah.
And this was around 1960.
Yeah, around that time. In '60 I was in Germany.
Yeah. And while you were in Germany in -
I stayed in Germany three years and a half in Hamburg, and two years in Mannheim [?]. And that was a period of the Cigalle too. And then I went back to the Cigalle again -
Right -
after that. Lasted three years and a half, that's in '63 and you know, [ ]. And I worked all over Germany and many, many other countries but mostly Germany, see. And I lived in Hamburg.
Was the offer of work for you as a single or as a soloist the reason why you were willing to leave your favorite capital of Europe, Paris, I mean -
Yeah.
Were you in - and you bought a car in Germany to go back to the States, not to go back to Paris so you still hadn't made your -
No, not then, no -
You still hadn't even made a committment to -
No -
figure you were staying over.
When I was in Germany the three years and a half, Hamburg, I bought my car in
